question.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | ${e}^{3}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $3$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}\frac{3{ln}^{2}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}{ln}^{2}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{3}{u}^{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\cdot \frac{{u}^{3}}{3}\,{|}_{0}^{3} \\  & ={u}^{3}\,{|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =({3}^{3}-{0}^{3}) \\  & =27-0 \\  & =27\end{aligned}
$$
